mainTopic: Whether a returning husband may presume his wife is טהורה, and the rule that a doubt cannot override a certainty
overview: The משנה taught that a husband coming back from a trip may assume his wife is טהורה. רב הונא limits this to a woman whose cycle depends on days plus an action such as jumping. A woman with a cycle of days alone is forbidden, because he holds וסתות are דאורייתא. רבה בר בר חנה permits even a cycle of days alone, because he holds וסתות are דרבנן. רבי יוחנן rules that a husband may count his wife's cycle days and then be with her. רבי אבא explains that this works even for a shy young girl, since it is only a double doubt: maybe she never saw blood, and even if she did, maybe she immersed. If she definitely saw blood, she is forbidden, because אין ספק מוציא מידי ודאי. The גמרא challenges this rule from a dead חבר's produce and answers it in two ways. It then challenges the rule again from a stillborn baby thrown into a pit, and begins to reread that ברייתא, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רב הונא limits the rule to a cycle of days plus jumps
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא says the משנה's presumption of purity applies only when her וסת depends on days and also on jumping. With a cycle of days alone, she is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: They only taught this when she does not have a cycle of days alone. Rather, it is when she has a cycle of days and jumps. Since the matter depends on an action, we can say she did not jump and so did not see blood. But if she has a cycle of days alone, she is forbidden to be with her husband.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא narrows the משנה's rule that a returning husband may assume his wife is טהורה. He says it only works when her period depends on doing something, like jumping.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If her period comes only on a certain day plus jumping, the husband can assume she did not jump, so no blood came. If her period depends on the day alone, that day came no matter what, so we cannot assume she stayed טהורה. In that case she needs a בדיקה first.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman's fixed menstrual pattern, which lets her expect when her period will come
A cycle set only by the calendar, on a fixed day
Jumps; a physical action that, together with the day, brings on her period

steps.confusionAlert: Do not get the cases backwards. The cycle of days plus jumps is the easier case, where she is permitted. The cycle of days alone is the stricter case, where she is forbidden.

phrases.english: They only taught this
phrases.notes: This is רב הונא speaking about the משנה's rule that a husband back from a trip may assume his wife is טהורה.

phrases.english: where she does not have a cycle of days alone
but rather she has a cycle
of days and of jumps
phrases.notes: Her period comes on a certain day, but only if she also jumps.

phrases.english: since the matter depends on an action
say she did not jump and did not see blood
but if she has a cycle of days alone
she is forbidden to have relations

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁאֵין לָהּ וֶסֶת לְיָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the משנה's rule about husbands returning from a trip
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The presumption of purity applies only to a woman whose וסת depends on days and jumps. A woman with a cycle of days alone is forbidden once that day arrives.

steps.title: רב הונא's reason: the concern for a cycle is Torah law
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רב הונא holds וסתות are דאורייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds that the concern about her expected period is Torah law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reason behind רב הונא's strict ruling. He holds that the concern about her expected period comes from the Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the concern about a וסת is Torah law, then once her day arrives she is in real doubt about Torah-level טומאה. A doubt about Torah law is treated strictly, so she must check before being with her husband.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds; introduces someone's underlying reasoning
The concern about her expected period is Torah law

phrases.english: He holds that cycles are a Torah-law concern
phrases.notes: "He" means רב הונא from the previous step.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason for רב הונא's ruling in step 1
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב הונא holds וסתות are דאורייתא, so a woman with a cycle of days alone is in Torah-level doubt on her day.

steps.title: רבה בר בר חנה permits even a cycle of days alone
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה says even a woman with a cycle of days alone is permitted, because he holds וסתות are דרבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה says: even if she has a cycle of days alone, she is permitted. He holds that the concern about her expected period is only rabbinic.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר בר חנה argues with רב הונא. He says the husband may rely on the presumption of purity even when her cycle depends on days alone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole argument comes down to one question: is the concern about a וסת from the Torah or from the רבנן? If it is only rabbinic, we do not assume she actually saw blood. So even though she should have checked, the חזקת טהרה still holds.

keyTerms.meaning: Rabbinic law, not from the Torah

steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא holds וסתות are דאורייתא, so she is forbidden. רבה בר בר חנה holds they are דרבנן, so she is permitted. The level of the וסת concern decides the case.

phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Chana says:

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ יֵשׁ לָהּ וֶסֶת לְיָמִים — מוּתֶּרֶת,
phrases.english: even if she has a cycle of days alone, she is permitted
He holds that cycles are a rabbinic concern

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ יֵשׁ לָהּ וֶסֶת לְיָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב הונא's limitation and its reasoning
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even a woman with a cycle of days alone remains permitted, because וסתות are דרבנן.

steps.title: A husband may calculate his wife's cycle days and be with her
steps.stepSummary: רב שמואל, in the name of רבי יוחנן, rules that the husband of a woman with a וסת may count her cycle days and then be with her.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמואל said in the name of רבי יוחנן: a woman who has a fixed cycle — her husband calculates the days of her cycle, and then he may be with her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new statement from רבי יוחנן. A husband whose wife has a fixed וסת may figure out her cycle days on his own and then be with her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because her cycle is fixed, the husband can work out when her period would have come and when it would have ended. He may then rely on that count and be with her without asking her.

keyTerms.meaning: And he may be with her (have relations)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב שְׁמוּאֵל מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rav Shmuel said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
a woman who has a fixed cycle
her husband calculates the days of her cycle
and he may be with her

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שְׁמוּאֵל מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: אִשָּׁה שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהּ וֶסֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a new ruling from רבי יוחנן about a woman with a fixed וסת
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The husband of a woman with a fixed וסת may calculate her cycle days and then be with her.

steps.title: Does the leniency apply even to a shy young girl?
steps.stepSummary: רב שמואל בר ייבא asks רבי אבא whether רבי יוחנן's leniency applies even to a young girl who is embarrassed to go immerse.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמואל בר ייבא asked רבי אבא: Did רבי יוחנן really say this even about a young girl who is too shy to go immerse?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question is asked about רבי יוחנן's ruling from step 4. Does it still hold when the wife is a young girl who might be too shy to go to the מקוה?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן allowed the husband to simply count the days and be with her, assuming everything was handled properly. With a shy young girl, that assumption is weaker, because she may never have gone to immerse. So the question is whether the leniency still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: A young girl (here, a young wife)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר יֵיבָא לְרַבִּי אַבָּא:
phrases.english: Rav Shmuel bar Yeiva said to Rabbi Abba:
Did Rabbi Yochanan say [this]
even about a young girl who is embarrassed to immerse?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר יֵיבָא לְרַבִּי אַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests how far רבי יוחנן's ruling in step 4 reaches.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does רבי יוחנן's leniency include a young wife who may have been too shy to immerse?

steps.title: The leniency is only for a double doubt
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא answers that רבי יוחנן never permitted a woman who definitely saw blood. He only spoke where it is unsure whether she saw, and even if she did, she may have immersed.
steps.simpleTranslation: He answered: Did רבי יוחנן say his ruling about a woman who definitely saw blood? He only said it where we don't know if she saw or not. And even if she did see, we can say she immersed.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא answers by narrowing רבי יוחנן's ruling. It only covers a case where we don't even know that she saw blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here there are two doubts stacked together. Maybe she never saw blood at all, and even if she did, maybe she immersed. That is why even a shy young girl is permitted: the leniency never depended only on her going to immerse.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say...? (introduces a rejected assumption)
Unsure whether she saw or did not see

phrases.english: He said to him:
Is that to say that [about a case where] she definitely saw
Rabbi Yochanan said [his ruling]?!
Say that Rabbi Yochanan said [it]
where it is unsure whether she saw, unsure whether she did not see,
and if you will say she saw,
say that she immersed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַטּוּ וַדַּאי רָאֲתָה מִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5 by limiting רבי יוחנן's case.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes, even a young girl is permitted, because רבי יוחנן only spoke where it is unsure whether she saw blood. Even if she saw, she may have immersed.

steps.title: A doubt cannot override a certainty
steps.stepSummary: If she definitely saw blood, we cannot assume she immersed, because אין ספק מוציא מידי ודאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if she definitely saw blood, who says she immersed? That is a doubt against a certainty, and a doubt cannot override a certainty.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא finishes his answer by explaining why a woman who definitely saw blood would be forbidden. He uses the general rule that a doubt cannot override a certainty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If she definitely saw blood, her impurity is certain, and the only doubt is whether she immersed. One single doubt is too weak to push aside a known fact. This rule is what the גמרא will challenge next.

keyTerms.meaning: A doubt does not take something out of a certain status

steps.whyThisMatters: אין ספק מוציא מידי ודאי is a basic rule used throughout ש״ס for weighing doubts against known facts.

phrases.english: But [where] she definitely saw,
who is to say that she immersed?
It is a doubt against a certainty,
and a doubt does not take [something] out of the hands of a certainty.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל וַדַּאי רָאֲתָה מִי יֵימַר דְּטָבְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי אבא's answer by giving the reason the definite case is forbidden.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Where she definitely saw blood, the doubt about immersion cannot override that certainty: אין ספק מוציא מידי ודאי.

steps.title: Challenge from a חבר who left produce
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the rule from a ברייתא. A dead חבר's produce is presumed tithed, even though it was certainly טבל and only possibly tithed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Doesn't a doubt override a certainty? But a ברייתא teaches: a חבר who died and left a storehouse full of produce, even produce from that very day, is presumed to be tithed. Here it was definitely טבל, and only possibly tithed, yet the doubt overrides the certainty!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the rule from step 7. It brings a ברייתא where a doubt seems to override a certainty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The produce of a חבר started out as definite טבל, and whether he tithed it before he died is only a doubt. Yet the ברייתא says it is presumed tithed. That looks like a doubt beating a certainty, which contradicts אין ספק מוציא מידי ודאי.

keyTerms.meaning: A person trusted to be careful about tithes and purity
From that very day (just brought in)
Produce from which tithes have not yet been taken

phrases.english: And not?
phrases.notes: Meaning: is it really true that a doubt never overrides a certainty?

phrases.english: But isn't it taught [in a ברייתא]:
A חבר who died
and left a storehouse full of produce,
even if they are from that very day,
they are presumed to be prepared (tithed).
But here, it is definitely טבל,
unsure if it was tithed, unsure if it was not tithed,
and the doubt comes and takes it out of the hands of the certainty!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the principle stated in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule אין ספק מוציא מידי ודאי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the ברייתא, produce that was certainly טבל is presumed tithed based only on a doubt, so a doubt does seem to override a certainty.

steps.title: First answer: the חבר case is certainty against certainty
steps.stepSummary: The חבר's produce is not a case of doubt against certainty. We are certain he tithed, because a חבר never lets untithed food leave his hands.
steps.simpleTranslation: There it is certain against certain. This follows רב חנינא חוזאה, who said: we presume a חבר never lets anything leave his hands that has not been properly tithed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 8. In the חבר case, his tithing is not a doubt at all; it is also a certainty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 said the produce was certainly טבל and only possibly tithed. This answer upgrades the 'possibly tithed' side into a 'certainly tithed' side, based on the חזקה of a חבר. So the case is certainty against certainty, and the rule אין ספק מוציא מידי ודאי is not touched.

keyTerms.meaning: Certainty against certainty: both sides are definite
A legal presumption we rely on

phrases.english: There, it is certain against certain,
phrases.notes: The food was certainly טבל, but the חבר also certainly tithed it, so neither side is a doubt.

phrases.english: in line with Rav Chanina Choza'ah,
as Rav Chanina Choza'ah said:
There is a presumption about a חבר
that he does not let out from under his hand
anything that is not properly tithed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 8 by redefining the חבר case as certainty against certainty.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: the 'doubt' side is really a certainty
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The חבר's produce was certainly טבל and only possibly tithed, so a doubt beat a certainty.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because of the חזקה about a חבר, his tithing is also certain. Two certainties are in play, so the rule is not broken.

steps.title: Second answer: the חבר case is doubt against doubt
steps.stepSummary: Alternatively, even the 'certain טבל' side is really a doubt. The produce may never have become obligated in מעשר, using רבי אושעיא's trick of bringing grain in with its chaff.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or you can say: it is doubt against doubt, in line with רבי אושעיא. He said a person may use a trick with his grain: he brings it in still in its chaff, so that his animal can eat it and it is exempt from מעשר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different answer to the same challenge. This time it says the 'certain' side was never really certain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first answer made the tithing certain. This answer instead makes the obligation itself doubtful. Grain brought home in its chaff may be exempt from מעשר, so we don't know the produce was ever truly טבל. That makes it doubt against doubt, and the rule about doubt versus certainty does not apply.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And if you want, say': introduces a second, alternative answer
Doubt against doubt: both sides are uncertain
Uses a legal trick or workaround
Chaff, the husks around the grain

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבי אושעיא lets a person cheat on tithes for his own eating. The trick only covers grain brought in still in its chaff for his animal to eat; at that stage the obligation of מעשר has not yet taken hold.

phrases.english: And if you want, say:
it is doubt against doubt,
phrases.notes: We're unsure he tithed, and we're also unsure the food ever needed tithing.

phrases.english: in line with Rabbi Oshaya,
as Rabbi Oshaya said:
A person may use a trick with his grain
and bring it in still in its chaff,
so that his animal can eat it
and it is exempt from tithe.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second, independent answer to the challenge of step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: the 'certain' side is really a doubt
steps.terutzMaskana: The produce may have been exempt from the start, so both sides are doubts and the rule does not apply.

steps.title: New challenge: the stillborn baby thrown into a pit
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the rule again from a ברייתא. A maidservant threw a stillborn into a pit, and a כהן leaned over the pit to see whether it was a boy or a girl.
steps.simpleTranslation: And still, does a doubt not override a certainty? But a ברייתא teaches: there was a story about the maidservant of an olive harvester in רימון. She threw a stillborn baby into a pit, and a כהן came and looked in to find out whether it was male or female.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new attack on the rule 'a doubt does not override a certainty.' Here it sets up the story; the ruling that makes the challenge comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We know for certain a dead body was thrown into the pit. If it was still there, the כהן became טמא by leaning over it. So this case starts with a certain source of impurity.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And still': the problem has not gone away

phrases.aramaic: וְאַכַּתִּי אֵין סָפֵק מוֹצִיא מִידֵי וַדַּאי?
phrases.english: And still, does a doubt not override a certainty?
But isn't it taught in a ברייתא:

phrases.aramaic: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּשִׁפְחָתוֹ שֶׁל מַסִּיק אֶחָד בְּרִימּוֹן,
phrases.english: There was a story with the maidservant of a certain olive harvester in Rimon,
who threw a stillborn baby into a pit,
and a כהן came and peered into it
to know whether it was male or female.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַכַּתִּי אֵין סָפֵק מוֹצִיא מִידֵי וַדַּאי? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the two answers save the rule from the חבר case, the גמרא brings a new source against it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule of step 7: אין ספק מוציא מידי ודאי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There was certainly a corpse in the pit. If the Sages rule the כהן pure because of a mere possibility that it was removed, then a doubt overrode a certainty.

steps.title: The Sages rule the כהן pure because animals may have dragged the body away
steps.stepSummary: The Sages ruled the כהן טהור, since martens and hyenas were common there and may have carried off the body before he looked.
steps.simpleTranslation: The story came before the Sages, and they ruled him pure, because martens and hyenas are common there.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with the Sages' ruling that the כהן is טהור, because animals may have taken the body. This ruling is what drives the challenge, and the next step spells the challenge out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The body being in the pit was certain. Its removal by animals was only a possibility. Yet the Sages let that possibility decide the case, which seems to contradict אין ספק מוציא מידי ודאי.
steps.whatToRemember: The rule 'a doubt cannot override a certainty' now faces a hard case. A כהן was ruled pure because animals may have removed a body that was certainly in the pit.

phrases.english: And the story came before the Sages,
and they declared him pure,
because martens and hyenas
are common there.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא begun in step 11 with the ruling that powers the challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule of step 7: אין ספק מוציא מידי ודאי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The Sages ruled the כהן טהור only because martens and hyenas might have dragged away a body that was certainly thrown into the pit, so a doubt seems to override a certainty.

steps.title: The pit case looks like a doubt beating a certainty
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא states the problem outright. It was certain the maidservant threw a נפל into the pit, and only a doubt whether animals dragged it away. Yet the doubt won.
steps.simpleTranslation: But here it is certain she threw a stillborn into the pit. It is only a doubt whether animals dragged it away or not. And still the doubt comes and overrides the certainty!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the challenge from the pit story in steps 11-12. It points out that the ruling of טהור seems to let a doubt push aside a certainty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The certain fact is that a נפל went into the pit. The only doubt is whether martens or hyenas carried it off before the כהן looked. By calling the כהן טהור, the חכמים let that doubt override the certain fact, which goes against the rule that a ספק cannot remove a ודאי.
steps.confusionAlert: The 'certainty' here is not that the כהן became טמא. It is that a body was thrown into the pit. The doubt is only whether the body was still there.

phrases.english: But here, where it is certain she threw a stillborn,
it is a doubt whether they dragged it away or did not drag it away,
and yet a doubt comes and takes us out of a certainty!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out why the ruling in step 12 contradicts the rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that a ספק cannot override a ודאי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A certain fact (a body in the pit) was set aside because of a doubt (maybe animals took it), and the כהן was ruled טהור.

steps.title: Changing how we read the pit story
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins its answer by saying we should not read the ברייתא as 'she threw a stillborn into a pit.' It starts to give a different wording, which continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do not say 'she threw a stillborn into a pit.' Rather, say...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is starting its answer by rereading the ברייתא. This line sets up the new wording, which comes right after.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge only works if it was certain a stillborn was thrown in. By changing the wording, the גמרא will take away that certainty. If both sides are doubts, the rule about doubt and certainty is not broken.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Do not say... rather say': the גמרא rereads a source to change its meaning

phrases.english: Do not say "she threw a stillborn into a pit,"
rather, say

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא תֵּימָא ״הֵטִילָה נֵפֶל לְבוֹר״, אֶלָּא אֵימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the challenge of step 13 by rereading the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the source (לא תימא אלא אימא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא described a certain stillborn thrown into the pit.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא will be read so that it is not certain a stillborn was thrown in (this continues on the next amud).
